content:
Involved in national security case, the bookstore 'Liuxia Bookhouse' has been closed for over a month. Today (25th), it announced it will cease operations on 30 August as originally scheduled. The bookstore will resume its final operations from tomorrow (26th) to Sunday (30th) for five consecutive days, from 1pm to 9pm, to clear stock.

Liuxia Bookhouse posted a farewell message on social media, saying: 'Four years pass like a snap of the fingers, yet as flowers fall, we remain acquainted. In books, one finds no golden house; in books, one sees no fair lady. Why force the realization of lifelong ambitions? Boiling wine and chatting joyfully is enough. Facing this letter, tears stream down, I know not what I say, only a word of gratitude. Take care.'

Established four years ago, Liuxia Bookhouse announced its closure at the end of August last month. The following day, national security officers arrived and accused it of suspected sedition under Article 23, arresting three people from the bookstore, who were alleged to have committed sedition under Article 23. Two people from Tin Yuen Bookstore were also arrested in the same case. The 50-year-old Tin Yuen Bookstore also announced at the end of last month that it would close after its lease expires. The publication involved in the case is reportedly 'Red Flowers Bloom: Identity and Belonging in the Xi Jinping Era' written by Chinese-American journalist Eileen Feng.

Liuxia Bookhouse was founded in 2022 by veteran media practitioner Shum Wan-wah and several former journalists from Stand News. At that time, media outlets such as Apple Daily, Stand News, and Citizen News had already ceased operations one after another. The bookstore was named 'Liuxia' (留下, meaning 'to stay') and 'Bookhouse' to signify 'leaving behind writing' (留下書寫). The store primarily focused on books related to news reporting and media, and also regularly held talks and author sharing sessions.

On the 14th of last month, Liuxia Bookhouse announced it would close on 30 August, stating that the unpredictable red line was also a reason for closure.
